```lua
 pprint("MOUNTS", liveupdate.get_mounts())
```

```lua
DEBUG:SCRIPT: MOUNTS,
{ --[[0x119667bf0]]
  1 = { --[[0x119667c50]]
    name = hash: [liveupdate],
    uri = "zip:/device/path/to/acchives/liveupdate.zip",
    priority = 5
  },
  2 = { --[[0x119667d50]]
    name = hash: [_base],
    uri = "archive:build/default/game.dmanifest",
    priority = -10
  }
}
```

issues.author: JCash
issues.body:
### Gamepad identification

This is a first part of updating how our gamepads are identified.
With this update, it's easier to identify the type of controller that was connected.
The gamepad connected event now also contains:
* `gamepad_guid` -- the 32 character guid
* `gamepad_guid_info`:

 Field     | Description
 --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------
 `vendor`  | USB vendor id. E.g. Nintendo 0x057e, Sony 0x054c, or Microsoft 0x045e
 `product` | USB product id
 `bus`     | How device is communicating. E.g.0x0003 for USB devices and 0x0005 for Bluetooth devices.
 `crc`     | SDL CRC16 signature, typically used when vendor and product ids are unavailable
 `version` | The device or firmware version

### New macOS/iOS gamepad backend
 
Also updated macOS/iOS support to use the `GameController` framework for better support of gamepads (e.g. Switch Pro controller)

Example project: https://github.com/defold/example-gamepad
issues.title: Added support for reporting Sdl Guid for connected gamepads

issues.author: JCash
issues.body:
This allows you to start an app via `adb` using extra command line arguments.
It is good for debugging different scenarios without having to build different .apk files for each one.
E.g. for testing different levels in isolation when doing a commit to your CI.

Note: It requires that the application is *debuggable* 

Example of how to launch an app with a different boot collection
```bash
adb shell am start \
    -n com.doman.myapp/com.dynamo.android.DefoldActivity \
    -a android.intent.action.MAIN \
    -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER \
    --esa com.dynamo.android.EXTRA_COMMAND_LINE_ARGUMENTS \
    "--config=bootstrap.main_collection=/main/levels/level1.collectionc"
```
issues.title: Added support for passing command line arguments to an Android app

issues.author: nanaktaev
issues.body:
New `render.set_blend_func_separate()` and `render.set_blend_equation_separate()` functions that provide separate control over color and alpha blend factors and equations. This enables advanced blending techniques such as 2D soft shadows (Slembcke technique) that require FUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT for the alpha channel while keeping FUNC_ADD for color.

**New API:**

```lua
-- Set separate blend factors for color and alpha channels
render.set_blend_func_separate(source_factor_color, destination_factor_color,
                               source_factor_alpha, destination_factor_alpha)

-- Set separate blend equations for color and alpha channels
render.set_blend_equation_separate(equation_color, equation_alpha)
```

**New constants:** `graphics.BLEND_EQUATION_ADD`, `graphics.BLEND_EQUATION_SUBTRACT`, `graphics.BLEND_EQUATION_REVERSE_SUBTRACT`, `graphics.BLEND_EQUATION_MIN`, `graphics.BLEND_EQUATION_MAX`.

Fully backwards compatible — existing `render.set_blend_func()` continues to work identically.
issues.title: Add render.set_blend_state() for separate blend factors and equations

issues.author: vlaaad
issues.body:
Now, the editor exposes a local, authenticated `/eval` endpoint for evaluating Lua code in the editor Lua runtime.

Simplest example:

```sh
curl \
  "http://localhost:$(cat .internal/editor.port)/eval" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat .internal/editor.token)" \
  --data "print('Hello from Lua') return 1, 'two', true"
# Hello from Lua
# => 1
# => two
# => true
```

Because `/eval` can run commands through `editor.execute`, requests must include the token from `.internal/editor.token`. This limits access to clients that also have filesystem access.

```sh
curl \
  "http://localhost:$(cat .internal/editor.port)/eval" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat .internal/editor.token)" \
  --data "editor.execute('git', 'status', '--short', { reload_resources = false })"
#  M game.project
```

Security is documented in `openapi.json`, so the only URL your coding agent needs is still `http://localhost:$(cat .internal/editor.port)/openapi.json`. For example:
```md
› use /eval endpoint and make a short report about the available functionality
• Thinking...
• Short Report

  `/eval` evaluates raw Lua in the Defold editor extension runtime.

  Available runtime functionality includes:

  - Standard Lua globals: `assert`, `pcall`, `load`, `require`, `io`, `os`, 
    `math`, `string`, `table`, `coroutine`, etc.
  - Defold editor API via `editor`, including:
      - resource inspection: `editor.resource_attributes`,
        `editor.properties`, `editor.get`
      - resource/project mutation APIs: `editor.transact`, 
        `editor.tx.set`/`add`/`remove`/`reorder`/`reset`/`clear`, `editor.save`
      - filesystem helpers: `editor.create_directory`, `editor.delete_directory`, 
       `editor.create_resources`
      - external command execution: `editor.execute`
      - browser/file helpers: `editor.browse`, `editor.open_external_file`,
        `editor.external_file_attributes`
      - UI construction/dialog APIs under `editor.ui`
      - preferences via `editor.prefs.get`/`set`/`is_set`
  - HTTP APIs via `http`, including `http.request` and `http.server.route`/`response`
  - Utility modules: `json.encode`/`decode`, `zip.pack`/`unpack`, 
    `zlib.deflate`/`inflate`, `localization`.
```
issues.title: Add `/eval` endpoint to editor server

issues.author: Jhonnyg
issues.body:
⚠️ BREAKING CHANGE ⚠️

The vertices for the `sprite`, `gui`, `tilegrid` and `particle` components are now unified with the rest of the components. The engine is now using counter-clockwise ordering of the vertices so that the normal of the primitive is pointing towards the camera. This means that you can use the same face culling parameters for all components.

Regarding breaking change:
This should only have an impact if you are using face culling for your components. In the default render script, we have enabled backface culling only for models but if your project is using backface culling for other components you might have to switch the front/back face using `render.set_cull_face(graphics.FACE_TYPE_BACK)`. The default cull face mode is FACE_TYPE_BACK, so you can also just remove the `render.set_cull_face` call
issues.title: Component primitive order unification

### Gamepad identification

This is a first part of updating how our gamepads are identified.
With this update, it's easier to identify the type of controller that was connected.
The gamepad connected event now also contains:
* `gamepad_guid` -- the 32 character guid
* `gamepad_guid_info`:

 Field     | Description
 --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------
 `vendor`  | USB vendor id. E.g. Nintendo 0x057e, Sony 0x054c, or Microsoft 0x045e
 `product` | USB product id
 `bus`     | How device is communicating. E.g.0x0003 for USB devices and 0x0005 for Bluetooth devices.
 `crc`     | SDL CRC16 signature, typically used when vendor and product ids are unavailable
 `version` | The device or firmware version

### New macOS/iOS gamepad backend
 
Also updated macOS/iOS support to use the `GameController` framework for better support of gamepads (e.g. Switch Pro controller)

Example project: https://github.com/defold/example-gamepad

issues.author: Jhonnyg
issues.body:
Two new script modules have been added to the engine: `material` and `compute`.

These modules expose runtime inspection and mutation APIs for material and compute resources, making it possible to read and update constants, samplers, textures, and material vertex attributes from Lua.

## Added Script Functions

### `material`

#### Inspect Material Resources

```lua
local attributes = material.get_vertex_attributes("/my_material.materialc")
-- attributes contain:
-- {
--     {
--         name = hash("attribute_name"),
--         value = vmath.vector4(...), -- or vmath.vector3, vmath.matrix4, number, or table
--         normalize = false,
--         data_type = graphics.DATA_TYPE_FLOAT,
--         coordinate_space = graphics.COORDINATE_SPACE_WORLD,
--         semantic_type = graphics.SEMANTIC_TYPE_COLOR
--     }
-- }

local samplers = material.get_samplers("/my_material.materialc")
-- samplers contain:
-- {
--     {
--         name = hash("sampler_name"),
--         type = graphics.TEXTURE_TYPE_2D,
--         u_wrap = graphics.TEXTURE_WRAP_REPEAT,
--         v_wrap = graphics.TEXTURE_WRAP_REPEAT,
--         min_filter = graphics.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR,
--         mag_filter = graphics.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR,
--         max_anisotropy = 1
--     }
-- }

local constants = material.get_constants("/my_material.materialc")
-- constants contain:
-- {
--     {
--         name = hash("constant_name"),
--         type = material.CONSTANT_TYPE_USER,
--         value = vmath.vector4(...) -- only for user constants; arrays return a table of values
--     }
-- }

local textures = material.get_textures("/my_material.materialc")
-- textures contain:
-- {
--     {
--         path = hash("/some_texture.texturec"), -- only when resource-backed
--         handle = hash(...),
--         width = 128,
--         height = 128,
--         depth = 1,
--         mipmaps = 1,
--         type = graphics.TEXTURE_TYPE_2D,
--         flags = graphics.TEXTURE_USAGE_FLAG_SAMPLE,
--         page_count = 1
--     }
-- }
```

#### Update Material Resources

```lua
material.set_vertex_attributes("/my_material.materialc", {
    attribute_name = {
        value = vmath.vector4(1, 0, 0, 1),
        data_type = graphics.DATA_TYPE_FLOAT,
        semantic_type = graphics.SEMANTIC_TYPE_COLOR,
        coordinate_space = graphics.COORDINATE_SPACE_WORLD,
        normalize = false
    },
    attribute_a = { value = vmath.vector4(1, 0, 0, 1) },
    attribute_b = { value = vmath.vector3(0, 1, 0) }
})

material.set_samplers("/my_material.materialc", {
    sampler_name = {
        min_filter = graphics.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR,
        mag_filter = graphics.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR,
        u_wrap = graphics.TEXTURE_WRAP_REPEAT,
        v_wrap = graphics.TEXTURE_WRAP_REPEAT,
        max_anisotropy = 1
    }
})

material.set_constants("/my_material.materialc", {
    constant_name = {
        value = vmath.vector4(1, 2, 3, 4),
        type = material.CONSTANT_TYPE_USER
    }
})

material.set_textures("/my_material.materialc", {
    sampler_name = "/some_texture.texturec"
})
```

### `compute`

Compute resources expose the same sampler, constant, and texture APIs as materials. They do not expose vertex attribute APIs.

#### Inspect Compute Resources

```lua
local samplers = compute.get_samplers("/my_compute.computec")
-- samplers contain the same shape of data as material.get_samplers()

local constants = compute.get_constants("/my_compute.computec")
-- constants contain the same shape of data as material.get_constants()

local textures = compute.get_textures("/my_compute.computec")
-- textures contain the same shape of data as material.get_textures()
```

#### Update Compute Resources

```lua
compute.set_samplers("/my_compute.computec", { ... })
-- set sampler data using the same table shape as material.set_samplers()

compute.set_constants("/my_compute.computec", { ... })
-- set constant data using the same table shape as material.set_constants()

compute.set_textures("/my_compute.computec", { ... })
-- set texture data using the same table shape as material.set_textures()
```

### `graphics`

The PR also exposes additional graphics constants used by these APIs, including vertex attribute data types, vertex semantic types, coordinate spaces, texture usage flags, texture types, texture formats, texture filters, texture wrap modes, and context feature flags.
issues.title: Material and compute script modules

issues.author: singhvishalkr
issues.body:
When decoding base64 strings that lack padding characters, `dmCrypt::Base64Decode` returns nil. This happens because mbedTLS's base64 decoder strictly requires padding, but many systems (particularly JWT implementations) omit padding per RFC 4648 section 3.2 which states that padding is not always required.

This issue can be observed while using the crypt extension with Nakama's JWT tokens. The server sends tokens without padding, and the decode fails silently.

The fix adds the missing `=` characters before passing the input to mbedTLS when the input length is not a multiple of 4. In addition, a test cases covering strings with and without padding was added to prevent regression.

The change should not affect consoles since it only modifies the mbedTLS path.
issues.title: Fix Base64Decode to handle input without padding

issues.author: Jhonnyg
issues.body:
#### Model re-centering during import ⚠️ BREAKING CHANGE ⚠️
We have removed the automatic model re-centering step from the Bob model import pipeline so imported glTF model positions are not altered. It also adjusts model transform handling so skinned/bone-parented meshes preserve local transforms while rigid meshes keep their flattened world placement. Both of these changes takes Defold closer to a "what you see is what you get" approach for 3D content.

The re-centering means that If your 3D content suddenly changes positions / orientation, this means that the content needs to be modified in an authoring package (e.g Blender) and then re-exported to .glb again. Most projects should be unaffected by this change, but there _is_ a change in behaviour when importing models now in order to fix other incorrectly placed objects.

#### Editor vs runtime preview inconsitency
The editor preview now mirrors the runtime transform behaviour more closely: models with assigned skeletons use skeleton-relative transforms, while models without skeleton resources use their local model transforms, with bounds updated to match the selected transform path.

#### Runtime GPU skinning fixes
Runtime rig/model handling was also adjusted so parentless root bones keep the inherited ancestor transform from the imported skeleton, and skinning matrices are only applied when the model is actually animating.
issues.title: Fixes model transform inconsistencies between the editor and runtime for imported glTF/glb models
